parsed.rationale: Every member declared on `AudioPlayerProtocol` (9 members: `eventStream`, `installRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `makeAudioBufferStream`, `play`, `removeRenderTap`, `state`, `stateStream`, `stop`) is also present verbatim on `TimeShiftablePlayer`, which additionally declares 6 time-shifting-specific members (`isAtLiveEdge`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `secondsBehindLive`, `seek`, `seekToLive`, `timePositionStream`). This is a textbook protocol-inheritance relationship: `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a strict superset of `AudioPlayerProtocol`. Both protocols live in the same package (`Playback`) and the same directory (`Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/`), so the inheritance declaration is a one-line change with no cross-package dependency implications. Conformers of `TimeShiftablePlayer` currently must re-satisfy all 9 base requirements redundantly; making `TimeShiftablePlayer` inherit from `AudioPlayerProtocol` eliminates that duplication and makes the capability hierarchy explicit.
